messages:
sara wang: Heads-up — rolling a small canary for b5-lite-8q + streaming with KV-cache enabled. Seeing a small but consistent funcall parse failure rate.
kevin m: Reproable locally. Failures manifest as JSON that parses in python but our strict schema validator rejects. Looks like non-printable trailing chars.
mohit: Dumped raw bytes from the model stream. Example payload: 
```
{"tool":"write_file","args":{"path":"/var/log/x","content":"done"}}\u0000\u0000\n
```
The \u0000 is literally in the stream. Only on quantized canaries.
lia: Interesting — do we see this on non-streaming responses?
sara wang: Good q. No, batch/non-stream returns look clean. This only shows up when continuous streaming + kv-cache + q8 path.
kevin m: Stack trace from runtime shows sanitized UTF8 decode handled, but our parser runs before the sanitizer for funcalls. So trailing NULs slip through into the schema validator.
triage-bot: alert: funcall-parse-failure-rate increased to 0.58% (canary b5-lite-8q) across last 10k invokes.
mohit: Hypothesis: quantized kernel pads output buffers with 0x00 to fill SSE/AVX blocks and streaming boundary cut leaves pads at the end of message.
lia: If true, short-term fix = post-stream trim of trailing NUL/CONTROL chars before schema validation. Longer term = fix kernel output or ensure sanitizer runs earlier.
sara wang: Proposed quick mitigation: add a lightweight sanitizer step in inference proxy: `json = re.sub(r"[\x00-\x1F]+$","",json)` before parse. Also add metric: `funcall_trailing_control_pct`.
kevin m: Agreed. Also want an experiment: run 10k requests across three variants: unquantized, q8, q4f16 — with streaming enabled — and bucket by response length to see signal.
mohit: I ran an initial 2k/variant sample. q8 had 0.6% trailing control chars, q4f16 0.12%, unquantized 0.01%. Looks correlated with buffer block size.
lia: Can we verify whether disabling KV-cache for a subset reduces it?
sara wang: Yes — that was the other data point: same model + q8 + streaming but KV-cache disabled -> failures drop to 0.02%. So interaction between kv prefixing and quant kernel pad.
kevin m: Action items:
- sara: open PR for runtime sanitizer (short patch) + add metric (ETA EOD).
- mohit: collect full 10k/variant run and attach sample of raw byte sequences (ETA tomorrow morning).
- lia: add canary config to disable kv-cache for a subset of hosts and run A/B (ETA 2 days).
- infra: consider gate for dedicated vs hosted (flag to disable streaming for q8 models until fix)
sara wang: Rolling the sanitizer patch now to canary group. If anyone sees regressions ping me.
kevin m: FWIW, regex to strip trailing control: `re.sub(r"[\x00-\x1F]+$","",s)` — simple but effective. We'll also add unit test that simulates padded chunks.
moHit: noted — will include python and C runtime reproducer.
lia: Also adding eval to the onboarding checklist: `streaming+kv-cache` smoke for any quantized variant.
sara wang: Thanks team. If sanitizer helps we'll promote to wider canary and schedule kernel fix with runtime team. :thumbsup:
kevin m: Logged follow-up issue: https://redwood.example/intern/ISSUE-ml-parse-nullpad (internal link)
triage-bot: closed? not yet — monitoring continues.
